transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

My thoughts feel all jumbled and I can’t keep my words or plans straight anymore, even for simple tasks I’ve done for years. It's just gotten so bad lately that I feel completely overwhelmed trying to get through the day.
Have you noticed these difficulties with your memory and thinking coming on gradually over a long period, or did they start relatively suddenly alongside a specific change in your mood?

They've been building up gradually for about a year now, ever since my husband's health got really bad. But they get much worse and more noticeable when I'm in one of my high, wired moods. During those times, my mind just races so fast that I can't keep track of any of my thoughts.
Besides these 'high, wired' periods, have you experienced distinct episodes of feeling extremely low, hopeless, or lacking energy for weeks at a time?

No, I haven't really experienced those kinds of deep, hopeless, or low depressive periods. My main struggles have been the opposite—with those wired, high-energy phases, my jumbled thoughts, and the voices. I don't really get down or lack energy, as I'm usually far too revved up and busy.

Have you ever been diagnosed with a medical condition, such as a brain injury, thyroid issue, or neurological disorder, or are you currently taking any prescription medications for a physical health problem?

No, I don't think I have any medical conditions like a brain injury or thyroid problems. I do have some medicines I'm supposed to take, but my mind has been so jumbled lately that I can't really remember what they're for.
Could you try to find the names of those medications you are taking, or perhaps bring the bottles to our next appointment so we can review them together?

I can try to find them and bring them in next time, doctor. But to be honest, I've been so scattered and jumbled lately that I often forget to take my own medicines, and I can't even keep track of where the bottles are. I'll have to see if my family can help me look for them.
When you hear these voices, do you hear them only when you are feeling 'wired' and high-energy, or do they also happen when your mood feels more stable and normal?

I hear them during both times, actually. Even during those quieter weeks when my mood feels more flat and I'm not rushing around, I still hear that man's voice telling me people are going to take my husband away.
Have you experienced these voices and the belief that people are going to take your husband away for at least six months, even during the times when your energy and mood are relatively stable?

Yes, I've been hearing that voice and feeling like they're trying to take my husband away for almost a year now, so definitely more than six months. Even during the quieter, flatter weeks when I'm not all wired up, I still hear him and stay convinced that my boss and the hospital are tracking and judging me.
Besides the belief about your husband, do you have other fixed, organized ideas about your boss or the hospital tracking and judging you that have persisted consistently for the past year?

Yes, for almost a year now, I've been absolutely convinced that my boss and the hospital are tracking my every move to judge if I'm a good enough caregiver. This belief is constant and never goes away, even during those quieter weeks when my mood is flat and I'm not feeling high or rushed. I just know they are watching me and talking about me behind my back.

Apart from these specific, persistent concerns about being watched or judged by your boss and the hospital, have you experienced other symptoms like disorganized speech, highly unusual behavior, or a significant decline in your ability to take care of your basic daily needs?

Yes, my words get so jumbled that I'll jump from talking about mops to church to my husband's insulin before trailing off, and I've been skipping meals and forgetting to shower. At work, I'll suddenly freeze in the hallway holding the vacuum or pace around talking to myself until someone snaps me out of it. It's just made it impossible to keep up with my daily routine.
Have you experienced any other symptoms, such as seeing things that aren't there or feeling as though your thoughts are being broadcast to others or inserted into your mind by an outside force?
No, I have never seen things that aren't really there. I also haven't ever felt like my thoughts are being broadcasted to other people or inserted into my mind by some outside force.
Have these episodes of disorganized speech and behavior occurred exclusively during your 'wired' high-energy phases, or do they also persist during the quieter weeks when your mood is stable?

I'm not quite sure and I haven't really paid close enough attention to whether the jumbled speech and freezing up happen during those quieter weeks. I mostly just notice those things when I am feeling really overwhelmed or busy. It's hard for me to keep track of exactly when it all happens.
During those quieter weeks when you are not feeling 'wired' or high-energy, do you still find yourself struggling to speak clearly or freezing up in your daily tasks?

During those quieter weeks, I definitely still hear that man's voice and feel like I'm being watched. But I'm not really sure or haven't paid close enough attention to whether the speech mixing or freezing up happens as much during those specific times.
When you are in those quieter, stable weeks, do you still find it difficult to perform basic self-care tasks like showering, eating, or keeping your living space organized?

Even during those quieter weeks, I still hear that man's voice and feel like the hospital is watching me. But I'm not really sure or haven't tracked closely whether keeping up with my showering and eating gets any easier or stays difficult during those times.

When you are in these quieter, stable weeks, do you find yourself feeling completely indifferent or withdrawn from others, or do you still have the same level of interest in your usual activities as you did before this started?

During those quieter weeks, my mood feels flat and I'm not rushing around, but I still remain completely withdrawn from my friends and church activities. Hearing that man's voice and feeling convinced that people are watching and judging me makes it impossible to feel like my old self or enjoy the things I used to do.
During those quieter weeks when you are not feeling 'wired', do you find that your thoughts are still disorganized or that you have difficulty expressing yourself clearly in conversation?

I'm not entirely sure if my thoughts and speech are as jumbled during those quieter weeks. During those flat or calmer periods, I am mostly consumed by the voices and the feeling of being watched, so I haven't really noticed if my words get as mixed up as they do when I'm in my high-energy, wired phases.
When you are in those quieter, stable weeks, do you find that your behavior is still noticeably odd or that you have trouble carrying out routine daily tasks like cooking or cleaning?

Yes, even during those quieter weeks when my mood is flatter, hearing that man's voice and feeling watched makes it very hard to focus. I still struggle to get through daily tasks, and I often end up leaving my cleaning half-done, skipping meals, or forgetting to shower.
When you are in these quieter weeks, is your speech still difficult for others to follow, or are you able to speak in a way that people can understand more clearly?

I'm not entirely sure if my speech gets any easier for others to understand during those quieter weeks. I haven't really noticed, because even when I'm calmer, I'm still so distracted by that man's voice and the constant feeling that I'm being watched.
When you are in those quieter weeks, do people around you ever tell you that your sentences don't make sense, or do they generally seem to understand the content of what you are saying?

I'm not really sure if people have trouble understanding me or if they say my sentences don't make sense during those quieter weeks. Even when I am calmer, I am still so focused on hearing that man's voice and feeling like I am being watched and judged.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with persistent, fixed delusional beliefs (persecutory) and auditory hallucinations that occur independently of mood episodes. While the patient describes periods of 'wired' energy, the core psychotic symptoms (hallucinations and delusions) persist during periods when the mood is described as 'flat' or 'quieter', and the symptoms have lasted for over a year, meeting criteria for schizophrenia.
